PROM, EPROM and EEPROM programming and erasure methods.

questions.prompt: Which memory is most commonly used for a CPU cache?

questions.option_a: Its capacitors lose charge over time

questions.accepted_answers:
Electrically Erasable Programmable Read Only Memory
Electrically Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory

questions.prompt: Which memory can normally be programmed only once?
Explain two reasons why SRAM is usually chosen for CPU cache instead of DRAM.
questions.model_answer: SRAM provides very fast access, which suits a CPU cache, and it does not require periodic refreshing while powered.
questions.grading_criterion:
1: State that SRAM provides fast access suitable for cache.
1: State that SRAM does not need periodic refresh while powered.
questions.student_guidance:
Consider access speed.
Consider refresh operations.

questions.prompt: A thermostat must keep its configuration after a power cut. Identify a suitable memory technology and explain why it is appropriate.
questions.model_answer: EEPROM is suitable because it is non-volatile and can be rewritten electrically when configuration settings change.
questions.grading_criterion:
1: Identify a suitable non-volatile programmable memory, such as EEPROM or flash.
1: Explain that stored data remains after power is lost.
1: Explain that configuration can be updated when required.
questions.student_guidance:
Think of a memory that survives power loss.
Describe what happens during a blackout.
Consider whether settings may change later.
